name: New York
summary: The largest city in the United States: five boroughs of dense neighborhoods tied together by a 24-hour subway, home to Wall Street, Broadway, world-class museums and food from everywhere.

curated-2026-10.title: New York places and neighborhoods written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move fast here: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical 2025 asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighborhood centers.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for New York (Central Park)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals for Central Park; refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available.

neighborhoods.name: Financial District
neighborhoods.summary: Wall Street, the World Trade Center and City Hall at the southern tip of Manhattan, with ferries leaving from the Battery.

neighborhoods.name: SoHo
neighborhoods.summary: Cast-iron loft buildings and cobbled side streets packed with flagship shops and galleries.

neighborhoods.name: Lower East Side
neighborhoods.summary: Old tenement blocks of immigrant history, now mixing delis, galleries and late-night bars, next to Chinatown.

neighborhoods.name: East Village
neighborhoods.summary: Walk-up apartments, cheap eats, dive bars and NYU students around Tompkins Square Park and St. Marks Place.

neighborhoods.name: Greenwich Village
neighborhoods.summary: Crooked tree-lined streets of townhouses, jazz clubs and cafes around Washington Square and NYU, running west into the West Village.

neighborhoods.name: Chelsea
neighborhoods.summary: Art galleries, the High Line, Chelsea Market and big tech offices on the West Side between the Meatpacking District and Hudson Yards.

neighborhoods.name: Flatiron and Union Square
neighborhoods.summary: Startup offices and showrooms around the Flatiron Building, Madison Square Park and the Union Square Greenmarket.

neighborhoods.name: Kips Bay and Murray Hill
neighborhoods.summary: East Side blocks of mid-rise apartments beside the hospital row on First Avenue, popular with young professionals and medical staff.

neighborhoods.name: Midtown
neighborhoods.summary: The skyscraper core: Times Square, the Theater District, Rockefeller Center, Grand Central and Penn Station, busiest on weekdays.

neighborhoods.name: Hudson Yards
neighborhoods.summary: A new district of glass towers, offices and a mall built over the West Side rail yards.

neighborhoods.name: Upper West Side
neighborhoods.summary: Prewar apartment buildings and brownstones between Central Park and Riverside Park, with Lincoln Center and the Natural History Museum.

neighborhoods.name: Upper East Side
neighborhoods.summary: Museum Mile on Fifth Avenue, Park Avenue co-ops and busier rental blocks toward the East River, plus a cluster of major hospitals.

neighborhoods.name: Morningside Heights
neighborhoods.summary: The academic neighborhood around Columbia University and the Cathedral of St. John the Divine.

neighborhoods.name: Harlem
neighborhoods.summary: Brownstone blocks with deep African American and Latino cultural history, centered on 125th Street and the Apollo.

neighborhoods.name: Williamsburg
neighborhoods.summary: Former warehouses turned waterfront towers, bars, music venues and restaurants one subway stop from Manhattan, with a large Hasidic community to the south.

neighborhoods.name: DUMBO
neighborhoods.summary: Cobbled streets of converted warehouses under the Manhattan and Brooklyn Bridges, beside Brooklyn Bridge Park.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Brooklyn
neighborhoods.summary: Brooklyn's civic and office center, now dense with rental towers, beside Fort Greene, Barclays Center and BAM.

neighborhoods.name: Park Slope
neighborhoods.summary: Brownstone streets of young families sloping down from Prospect Park.

neighborhoods.name: Bushwick
neighborhoods.summary: Warehouses covered in murals, artist lofts, late-night clubs and a long-standing Latino community.

neighborhoods.name: Coney Island
neighborhoods.summary: The seaside amusement district at the end of the subway lines, quiet in winter and packed on summer weekends.

neighborhoods.name: Astoria
neighborhoods.summary: A diverse, food-loving neighborhood of Greek tavernas, beer gardens and two-family houses near the East River.

neighborhoods.name: Long Island City
neighborhoods.summary: Glass towers on the Queens waterfront with Manhattan skyline views, plus warehouses, film studios and MoMA PS1.

neighborhoods.name: Flushing
neighborhoods.summary: A busy Chinese and Korean commercial center around Main Street, beside Flushing Meadows Corona Park with Citi Field and the US Open grounds.

neighborhoods.name: Concourse
neighborhoods.summary: Art Deco apartment houses along the Grand Concourse, a short walk from Yankee Stadium.

neighborhoods.name: Belmont (Arthur Avenue)
neighborhoods.summary: The Bronx's Little Italy of bakeries, butchers and red-sauce restaurants, between Fordham University and the Bronx Zoo.

transit.name: New York City Subway
transit.summary: The 24-hour MTA subway, with lettered and numbered lines across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

transit.name: MTA New York City buses
transit.summary: Local, Select Bus Service and express routes in all five boroughs; slow in Manhattan traffic.

transit.name: NYC Ferry
transit.summary: East River and harbor ferry routes linking Wall Street, Midtown, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and the Rockaways.

transit.name: Staten Island Ferry

transit.name: PATH

transit.name: Long Island Rail Road

transit.name: Metro-North Railroad
transit.summary: Commuter rail from Grand Central through Harlem and the Bronx to Westchester and Connecticut.

transit.name: Citi Bike
transit.summary: Docked bike share, including e-bikes, across Manhattan and much of Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

employers.summary: Restaurant group behind Gramercy Tavern and The Modern.

employers.name: New York City Public Schools
employers.summary: The country's largest school district, run from the Tweed Courthouse.

employers.name: City of New York
employers.summary: City agencies around City Hall and the Municipal Building.

employers.name: Metropolitan Transportation Authority
employers.summary: Runs the subway, buses and commuter railroads from offices at 2 Broadway.

employers.name: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
employers.summary: Runs the airports, bridges, tunnels, PATH and the region's container ports.

employers.name: Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom
employers.summary: Large law firm headquartered at One Manhattan West.

employers.name: Columbia University
employers.summary: Faculty, research and staff jobs on the Morningside campus.

employers.name: New York University
employers.summary: Faculty, research and staff jobs around Washington Square.

career_hubs.name: Midtown business district
career_hubs.summary: Corporate headquarters, law firms, Broadway, hotels and new towers from Hudson Yards to Park Avenue.

career_hubs.name: Financial District and Civic Center
career_hubs.summary: Banks, insurers, city government and the World Trade Center offices.

career_hubs.name: Silicon Alley
career_hubs.summary: Big tech offices on the West Side and startups around Flatiron and Union Square.

career_hubs.name: Garment District and fashion
career_hubs.summary: Showrooms, design studios and fabric shops in the West 30s, near FIT and Herald Square.

career_hubs.name: East Side hospital corridor
career_hubs.summary: Hospital rows along York and First Avenues, plus the Alexandria Center for Life Science.

career_hubs.name: Downtown Brooklyn and Long Island City
career_hubs.summary: Back offices, courts, colleges, film studios and warehouses just across the East River.

climate.summary: Humid subtropical: hot, humid summers with thunderstorms, pleasant springs and autumns, and cold winters with a few snowstorms most years.

months.note: Coldest month; snow and icy wind off the rivers.
Cold and gray; the snowiest month on average.
Changeable; early blossoms late in the month.
Mild and green; outdoor dining fills up.
Warm; beaches open Memorial Day weekend.
Hot and humid; many locals leave town.
Cool; leaves turn in the parks.

annual_events.name: New York Fashion Week
annual_events.summary: Runway shows and showroom presentations at venues around Manhattan each February and September.

annual_events.name: Tribeca Festival
annual_events.summary: Film festival with premieres and talks, centered on Tribeca in Lower Manhattan.

annual_events.name: NYC Pride March
annual_events.summary: The last Sunday in June, ending in the Village near the Stonewall Inn.

annual_events.name: Mermaid Parade
annual_events.summary: Costumed summer parade along the Coney Island boardwalk.

annual_events.name: Shakespeare in the Park
annual_events.summary: Free Public Theater productions at the Delacorte Theater in Central Park.

annual_events.name: SummerStage
annual_events.summary: Outdoor concerts in city parks, with its main stage in Central Park.

annual_events.name: US Open tennis
annual_events.summary: Two weeks of Grand Slam tennis around Labor Day at Flushing Meadows.

annual_events.name: West Indian American Day Carnival
annual_events.summary: Labor Day parade of Caribbean costumes and soca along Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn.

annual_events.name: Village Halloween Parade
annual_events.summary: Night-time costume parade up Sixth Avenue on October 31.

annual_events.name: New York City Marathon
annual_events.summary: Runners cross all five boroughs on the first Sunday of November and finish in Central Park.

annual_events.name: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
annual_events.summary: Giant balloons travel from Central Park West to Herald Square on Thanksgiving morning.

annual_events.name: Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree
annual_events.summary: The tree is raised in November, lit in early December and stays up into January.

annual_events.name: New Year's Eve in Times Square
annual_events.summary: The ball drop at midnight, watched by huge crowds penned in from mid-afternoon.

local_color.name: Bacon, egg and cheese
local_color.summary: The bodega breakfast: bacon, a fried egg and American cheese on a roll, ordered as "salt, pepper, ketchup" and eaten walking to the train.

local_color.name: Bodegas
local_color.summary: Corner delis that stay open late or all night, with a grill at the back, coffee, lottery tickets, everything from cat food to cold medicine, and often a resident cat.

local_color.name: A slice
local_color.summary: Thin, wide New York pizza sold by the slice from a counter, folded in half lengthwise to eat on the move.

local_color.name: Bagel with a schmear
local_color.summary: Boiled-then-baked bagels with cream cheese, or with lox, onion and capers from an appetizing store; locals have strong views on toasting.

local_color.name: Pastrami on rye
local_color.summary: Hot pastrami piled high on rye with mustard and a sour pickle on the side, the signature order at the old Jewish delis.

local_color.name: Chicken over rice
local_color.summary: The halal cart plate: chopped chicken or lamb over yellow rice with lettuce, white sauce and hot sauce, sold from street carts on Midtown corners.

local_color.name: Black-and-white cookie
local_color.summary: A big, soft, cakey cookie iced half vanilla and half chocolate, sold in delis and bakeries across the city.

local_color.name: Egg cream
local_color.summary: A soda-fountain drink with neither egg nor cream: chocolate syrup, milk and seltzer stirred until it foams.

local_color.name: "Coffee regular"
local_color.summary: At a deli or coffee cart, "regular" means with milk and sugar, not plain black.

local_color.name: Sidewalk etiquette
local_color.summary: Walk fast, keep to the right, never stop dead at the top of subway stairs, and step to the side before checking your phone or map.

local_color.name: "On line"
local_color.summary: New Yorkers wait "on line" rather than "in line", whether at the deli, the DMV or a sample sale.

local_color.name: "The city"
local_color.summary: To people in Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Staten Island, "going into the city" means going to Manhattan.

local_color.name: Stoop sitting and stoop sales
local_color.summary: Brownstone stoops become front porches in warm weather, with neighbors talking, kids playing and weekend stoop sales of books and old clothes.

local_color.name: New York Yankees
local_color.summary: The Bronx Bombers play baseball at Yankee Stadium; their pinstripes and interlocking NY are seen worldwide.

local_color.name: New York Mets
local_color.summary: Queens's National League baseball team plays at Citi Field in Flushing, with fans used to suffering and loyal anyway.

local_color.name: New York Knicks
local_color.summary: The NBA team plays at Madison Square Garden, where courtside seats draw celebrities and a long wait for a title is part of the identity.

local_color.name: New York Rangers
local_color.summary: One of the NHL's Original Six, playing hockey at Madison Square Garden.

local_color.name: Brooklyn Nets
local_color.summary: The NBA team that moved from New Jersey to Barclays Center in 2012, wearing black and white.

local_color.name: New York Liberty
local_color.summary: The WNBA team plays at Barclays Center and won its first championship in 2024.

local_color.name: Giants and Jets
local_color.summary: Both of New York's NFL teams play across the Hudson at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, and fans of each look down on the other.
